newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open at year high on Clinton victory.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open at year high on Clinton victory.

text.p: French shares soared to a year high at Wednesday's opening, rallying strongly on the back of Bill Clinton's return for a second term to the White House and the Republicans maintaining their hold on Congress, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.57 points or 0.85 percent at 2,205.89 at 0910 GMT, after opening up 0.45 percent.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,208 from 2,193 on Tuesday's close.
Tyremaker Michelin rose 3.18 percent to 259.70 francs on nine-month and third-quarter sales which were seen as healthy advances.
French car parts maker Valeo was steady, with a 0.34 percent gain to 303.60 francs.

One trader said there was some regret there had been no full buy-out offer, which would have pleased minorities, instead of holding company CGIP's purchase of a 20 percent stake from Cerus which held 28 percent of Valeo.
CGIP gained, while Cerus continued to slip.
Oil company Elf was up 2.20 francs to 424 among the top 10 turnover stocks. The oil major announced a merger of its U.K. refining with Chevron and Murphy Petroleum.
